chapter: Charlie Johnson, Willie Gant and the late 1920s
title: Charlie Holmes's failing eye and refusing to record
summary: Caldwell tries to coax Holmes out to recordings, thinks his eye trouble keeps him home, and compares Art Tatum.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Well, the main thing, Stanley, after he made that recording in '72, one of his eyes started to going bad, see? Well, last -- a year ago we (unintelligible) Doc Varner, and he called Doc because he did some recording for Doc, and Doc said to me, said, Happy, come on talk with Charlie. We all belong to the same club, the Friendly Fifty. I said, yeah, because Doc kept talking about he wanted to get him up there so he could do some recording.

So I said, oh, I said, let me talk to him. So I said, hey, what do you say, Buddy? Hey, Hap. I said, I'm coming by so we can -- want to bring you up there and got a little jam session. He wouldn't come. He won't come on the recording date either.
Charlie, went up to his -- got to go up there again sometime this week, sat there and talk with him and have a few smiles, and he just won't come out. You can't get him out.
Well, I know when I talked to him --
-- I don't know -- I said, I think you ought to well, I said (unintelligible) make some records. He said no. So when he made that one, I was really surprised because he --

His eye hadn't bothered him that much then. But just since '72 he got worse. And so Doc tried to get him -- him and I are good buddies. I go by and chew the rag with him, sit there and talk about old times. And I coat him (unintelligible), come on, I'm going to come by. We go for a little walk. But I think he's conscious of the fact that his eye, you know, I guess he want to feel like that he's a burden on somebody. But he shouldn't. Look at Art Tatum. Look at them fellows.
Yes. But, of course, that's true, but then he was more or less -- he had that more or less from the time he was a child, didn't he, Tatum?
I think -- he wouldn't say, but I think -- I think that it could be hereditary or either from being diabetic or something.
When you (unintelligible) start with it. Charlie
